$comment: $/cancel_request is the one method that belongs to neither peer, and its payload is the only place a JSON-RPC request identifier reaches the schema. The identifier is a value union: null, an integer or a string, told apart by shape rather than by a discriminant. Both types are generated unexported — a caller cancels by cancelling a context, and never names a request id.

cases.name: a numeric identifier
cases.why: the second arm, whose format decides its Go type

cases.name: a negative numeric identifier
cases.why: the format is int64, so the sign is not a constraint

cases.name: the null identifier
cases.why: the arm every other arm's decoder refuses, so it is tried first

cases.name: an identifier that is neither
cases.why: three arms and no discriminant: a value matching none of them belongs to nothing

cases.name: a fractional identifier
cases.why: the schema types this arm as an integer, and the reference implementation does not check that

divergence.because: The schema types this arm `{"type":"integer","format":"int64"}`, and 1.5 is not an integer. The reference implementation validates it as `z.number()` — it reaches for `z.int()` only where the schema also states a minimum, so most of its integer fields accept fractions. AGENTS.md says the schema wins, so this is refused here, and the difference belongs upstream rather than in a local dialect.

cases.name: no identifier
cases.why: the property is required: a cancellation with nothing to cancel is not a cancellation
